doc.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021

title: The trad jazz controversy
summary: Asked about 'trad', he says it lost foundations and the black influence and became a corny white-dominated style at Australian festivals.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Have you got enmeshed in the trad jazz controversy like what does trad jazz actually mean?
No I didn’t even realize there was a controversy. Please enlighten me.
Well if you hear about it, you know, if you hear about it don’t go there.
Is it the Dixieland reference? That word?

Yes it’s partly that, it’s partly like what is the Chicago school, the whole thing. It is a little hard to, trad jazz I don’t think gets the respect that other forms do for whatever reasons, but I sometimes think it’s because it’s too upbeat. Like people don’t think it’s serious because it’s so darn happy.

I think trad jazz went in a direction that I think removed some of the foundations of what it was about. I mean Louis Armstrong was such an ambassador for the New Orleans style. And then I think it kind of tends to have lost the — dare I say — the black influence and tended to be just the color of a bunch of white dudes you know, and certainly growing up for me, well I was Australian, not everyone that’s white in Australia plays jazz but you know you go to the festivals and there’s a lot of corny old guys playing, you know this kind of ricky-ticky stuff without a real connection to what you can hear on the records it kind of became a little less hip dare I say? But I’m not sure how to answer that. I think it’s a complicated question, isn’t it?
